changes.old:

changes.new:
1. You start a listing from a Magic Link sent to you, from the sell flow in the Platform's app, or from the Platform's Quick page.

  2. In the sell flow, the acceptance is set out directly above the publish button, with this EULA linked: "By tapping Publish now you confirm: I have read and accept the TrustSquare Seller Terms, and confirm all listing information is accurate. I understand that listings with inappropriate content will be permanently removed." Tapping "Publish now — I accept the Terms" is your acceptance.

  3. When you publish a saved draft — for example from a Magic Link or from your Seller Hub — the step headed "Almost live" shows this EULA in full. Once you have scrolled to the end, you must tick "I have read and accept the TrustSquare Seller Terms, and confirm all listing information is accurate" and "I understand that listings with inappropriate content will be permanently removed", and tap "Go live".

  4. If you save an edit to a listing, or publish from elsewhere in the app, before you have accepted this EULA, this EULA is shown in full on a Terms sheet: you must scroll to the end, tick the same two confirmations and tap "I accept".

  5. Unless you have already accepted this EULA, a listing saved on the Quick page is kept as a draft and goes live only after you have read and accepted this EULA in the Platform's app.

  6. If this EULA changes materially after you have accepted it, you are asked to accept it again, in the same way, the next time you publish or edit a listing.

  7. The Platform records your acceptance timestamp and EULA version number. This record is stored in the Platform's database and constitutes your binding agreement.

  8. Tapping "Publish now — I accept the Terms", "Go live" or "I accept" constitutes your electronic signature on this Agreement per Section 4 of the ECT Act.

changes.new:
5.3A Local Market — the Seller Pays

The Local Market is the category for selling physical items of every kind, locally and person to person. Its Introductions follow different rules from every other category:

  • Its own acceptance. Before your first Local Market listing goes live, the Platform's app shows you the Local Market terms and asks you to accept them, separately from your acceptance of this EULA. The date and time of that acceptance are recorded on your account.

  • The Seller pays; Buyers pay nothing. When the first Introduction request on a Local Market listing arrives, 1T is debited from the Seller's Tuppence balance, or 2T if the listing is boosted at that moment. This is charged once per listing: further requests on the same listing cost the Seller nothing more. If the Seller's balance is below the amount due, the request is refused. A Buyer pays nothing to request or receive a Local Market Introduction, and nothing is held from the Buyer's balance.

  • Declining or not answering. The Seller's payment is not refunded if the Seller declines a request or does not answer it. Not answering a Local Market Introduction carries no Trust Score penalty, and Section 4.9 and blocking cause B3 do not apply to it.

  • Buyer no-shows. If a Buyer does not follow through on an Introduction the Seller has accepted, the Seller may report it once, within 30 days of the Introduction. The Platform's staff then uphold or dismiss the report; where the Buyer can be reached by email, the Buyer is told of the report first and may give their side. If the report is upheld, 3 points are taken off the Buyer's Trust Score and, if the listing is not suspended, 1T is credited to the Seller's Tuppence balance. A dismissed report changes nothing.

  • Trust Score, suspension and ban. You may publish a Local Market listing whatever your Trust Score, and Buyers may filter Local Market listings by the Seller's Trust Score. If your Trust Score falls below 30 while an upheld complaint against you is on record, all your Local Market listings are suspended (hidden from Buyers) and are restored automatically once your score is 30 or more again. If you are suspended a second time within 90 days of an earlier suspension, a 30-day cooling-off period also applies: your Local Market listings stay suspended, and you cannot publish new ones, until it has ended and your score is 30 or more again. A third suspension, at any time, is a permanent ban from the Local Market. A suspension or ban takes no Tuppence from your balance and does not affect your listings in any other category.

For Local Market listings, this Section applies in place of Section 4.9 and of any provision of this EULA under which the Buyer pays for an Introduction or Tuppence is held from the Buyer's balance (including Sections 1.1, 2.6, 5.1, 5.4, 6.1 and 6.3). This Section is changed in the same way as the rest of this EULA (Section 15.1).
